newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish shares up slightly on support, volume down.
newsitem.headline: Turkish shares up slightly on support, volume down.

text.p: Istanbul shares edged higher on Wednesday due to technical support which emerged at the index's 1,550 level, but volume dived amid political concerns and the absence of moving expectations, brokers said.

The IMKB National-100 closed 1,582, up five points, or 0.32 percent from Tuesday when it plunged 4.48 percent on renewed political worries ahead of a National Security Council (MGK) meeting expected next week.
Trade volume further shrank to 19.75 trillion lira ($155 million) from Tuesday's 26.15 trillion ($206.3 million) and Monday's 40.73 trillion ($321.5 million).

"Both the trade range and volume were narrow because of the market's inspired state. Signs that political tension may again mount is affecting the market which may drift sideways with selective activity until the MGK meeting," said Ibrahim Basnur from Ar securities.

The coalition government's Islamist wing opposes a plan to raise compulsory education to eight years from five as part of measures put forward at the military-dominated MGK's February 28 meeting to clamp down on rising Islamist activism.
